cnd14:2.1: For those standing in the middle of the stream: the stream is said to be transmigration, coming, going, coming and going, time, destination, one existence after another, passing away, rebirth, reappearance, breaking up, birth, old age, and death.
cnd14:2.2: The first point of transmigration is not found, and the last point is not found;
cnd14:2.3: right in the middle of transmigration, beings stand firm, are established, cling, have approached, are attached, and are committed.
cnd14:3.1: How is the first point of transmigration not found?
cnd14:3.2: It is not so that the cycle has turned for so many births, and beyond that does not turn. In this way, too, the first point of transmigration is not found.

cnd14:6.2: “Transmigration, mendicants, has no known beginning. No first point is found of sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, covered by ignorance and fettered by craving.
cnd14:6.3: For such a long time, mendicants, suffering has been undergone, agony has been undergone, and disaster has been undergone, swelling the cemeteries.
cnd14:6.4: This is quite enough, mendicants, to become disillusioned with all conditions, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be freed.”
cnd14:6.5: In this way, too, the first point of transmigration is not found.
cnd14:7.1: How is the last point of transmigration not found?
cnd14:7.2: It is not so that the cycle will turn for so many births, and beyond that will not turn. In this way, too, the last point of transmigration is not found.
cnd14:7.3: So many hundreds of births, so many thousands of births, so many hundreds of thousands of births …
cnd14:7.4: so many ten millions of births, so many hundreds of ten millions of births, so many thousands of ten millions of births, so many hundreds of thousands of ten millions of births, so many years, so many hundreds of years, so many thousands of years, so many hundreds of thousands of years, so many ten millions of years, so many hundreds of ten millions of years, so many thousands of ten millions of years, so many hundreds of thousands of ten millions of years, so many eons, so many hundreds of eons, so many thousands of eons, so many hundreds of thousands of eons, so many ten millions of eons, so many hundreds of ten millions of eons, so many thousands of ten millions of eons, so many hundreds of thousands of ten millions of eons: it is not so that the cycle will turn for them, and beyond that will not turn. In this way, too, the last point of transmigration is not found.
cnd14:7.5: In this way, the first point of transmigration is not found, and the last point is not found, and beings stand firm, are established, cling, have approached, are attached, and are committed right in the middle of transmigration—
cnd14:7.10: Kappa: this is that brahmin’s name … an expression—
cnd14:8.1: When a terrifying flood has arisen: when the flood of sensual desire, the flood of continued existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance have arisen, originated, come into being, been produced, and appeared.
cnd14:8.2: Terrifying: fear of birth, fear of old age, fear of sickness, fear of death—
cnd14:9.1: Overwhelmed by old age and death: those touched by old age, overwhelmed, enveloped, and afflicted.
cnd14:9.2: Those touched by death, overwhelmed, enveloped, and afflicted, pursued by birth, spread over by old age, overpowered by sickness, struck down by death, without protection, without shelter, without refuge, who have become without refuge—
cnd14:10.1: Declare an island, good fellow: speak, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal an island, protection, shelter, refuge, destination, and final resort.
cnd14:10.2: Good fellow: this is a friendly word, a respectful word, a form of address expressing respect and deference, that is, good fellow—
cnd14:11.3: Explain an island: tell, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal an island, protection, shelter, refuge, destination, and final resort—
cnd14:12.1: So that this might not occur again: so that this suffering might cease right here, be stilled, come to an end, and be calmed; so that suffering with renewed rebirth-linking might not come into being; and so that it might not be born, originate, come into being, or be produced in the sensual realm, the realm of form, or the formless realm; in sensual existence, existence in form, or formless existence; in percipient existence, non-percipient existence, or existence of neither perception nor non-perception; in one-aggregate existence, four-aggregate existence, or five-aggregate existence; in a further destination, rebirth, or rebirth-linking; in existence, in transmigration, or in the cycle.
cnd14:12.2: Might cease right here, be stilled, come to an end, and be calmed—
cnd14:15.1: For those standing in the middle of the stream: the stream is said to be transmigration, coming, going, coming and going, time, destination, one existence after another, passing away, rebirth, reappearance, breaking up, birth, old age, and death.
cnd14:15.2: The first point of transmigration is not found, and the last point is not found.
cnd14:15.3: Right in the middle of transmigration, beings stand firm, are established, cling, have approached, are attached, and are committed.
cnd14:16.1: How is the first point of transmigration not found …
cnd14:16.2: this is how the first point of transmigration is not found.
cnd14:16.3: How is the last point of transmigration not found …
cnd14:16.4: this is how the last point of transmigration is not found.
cnd14:16.5: In this way, the first point of transmigration is not found, and the last point is not found.
cnd14:16.6: Right in the middle of transmigration, beings stand firm, are established, cling, have approached, are attached, and are committed—
cnd14:16.9: Kappa: the Blessed One addresses that brahmin by name.
cnd14:16.10: Blessed One: this is a term of respect … a designation based on realization, that is, Blessed One—
cnd14:17.1: When a terrifying flood has arisen: when the flood of sensual desire, the flood of continued existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance have arisen, originated, come into being, been produced, and appeared.
cnd14:17.2: Terrifying: fear of birth, fear of old age, fear of sickness, fear of death—
cnd14:18.1: Overwhelmed by old age and death: those touched by old age, overwhelmed, enveloped, and afflicted, touched by death, overwhelmed, enveloped, and afflicted, pursued by birth, spread over by old age, overpowered by sickness, struck down by death, without protection, without shelter, without refuge, who have become without refuge—
cnd14:19.1: I declare an island to you, Kappa: I speak, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal an island, protection, shelter, refuge, destination, and final resort—
cnd14:22.3: the possession of greed, the possession of hate, the possession of delusion, the possession of conceit, the possession of views, the possession of corruptions, the possession of misconduct;
cnd14:22.4: the giving up of possession, the stilling of possession, the letting go of possession, the calming of possession: the deathless extinguishment—
cnd14:22.6: Not taking up: taking up is said to be craving.
cnd14:22.7: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd14:22.8: The giving up of taking up, the stilling of taking up, the letting go of taking up, the calming of taking up: the deathless extinguishment—
cnd14:23.1: This island, with nothing further: this is the island, protection, shelter, refuge, destination, and final resort.
cnd14:23.2: With nothing further: beyond that, there is no other island.
cnd14:23.3: Indeed, that island is thus the foremost, the best, the most excellent, the chief, the supreme, and the finest—
cnd14:24.1: I call it extinguishment: vāna is said to be craving.
cnd14:24.2: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd14:24.3: The giving up of vāna, the stilling of vāna, the letting go of vāna, the calming of vāna: the deathless extinguishment.
cnd14:24.4: Iti: this is a joining of words, a combining of words, a completion of words, a coming together of syllables, a smoothness of phrasing, and the sequence of words—
cnd14:24.6: I call: I speak, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal—
cnd14:25.1: The ending of old age and death: the giving up, stilling, letting go, and calming of old age and death, the deathless extinguishment—
cnd14:28.3: That is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd14:28.4: Having understood: having understood, known, weighed up, examined, clarified, and made clear that “all conditions are impermanent” …
cnd14:28.5: having understood, known, weighed up, examined, clarified, and made clear that “whatever is liable to arise, all of that is liable to cease.”
cnd14:28.8: when they develop mindfulness meditation by observing an aspect of the body, they are mindful …
cnd14:29.2: Having seen the Dhamma: they have seen the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, weighed up the Dhamma, examined the Dhamma, made the Dhamma clear, and clarified the Dhamma.
cnd14:29.3: Fully quenched: quenched because greed has been extinguished, because hate …
cnd14:29.4: because all unskillful choices have been calmed, settled, stilled, burned out, quenched, and tranquilized, they are peaceful, serene, stilled, quenched, and tranquil—
cnd14:30.2: Māra: he is Māra, the Dark One, the Ruler, the Ender, Namuci, the Kinsman of the Negligent.
cnd14:30.3: They don’t fall under Māra’s sway: they do not come under Māra’s power, and Māra does not exercise power over them.
cnd14:30.4: Having overcome, subdued, overwhelmed, exhausted, and crushed Māra, Māra’s faction, Māra’s snare, Māra’s hook, Māra’s bait, Māra’s domain, Māra’s dwelling, Māra’s range, and Māra’s bonds, they live, dwell, proceed, keep going, maintain, sustain, and carry on—
cnd14:31.1: They are not Māra’s followers: they would not be Māra’s retainers, attendants, or servants;
cnd14:31.2: they would be the Buddha, the Blessed One’s retainers, attendants, and servants—
cnd14:33.2: Sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher, and I am a disciple.
